"""Pydantic models for the dataset, schema-version and lineage APIs."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StrictBool, StrictInt, StrictStr


class DatasetCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Unique, non-empty dataset name")
    description: str = Field(default="", description="Optional human description")


class Dataset(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    description: str
    created_at: str


class FieldSpec(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Unique, non-empty field name within the version")
    type: str = Field(description="Field type, e.g. 'string' or 'integer'")
    nullable: bool


class SchemaVersionCreate(BaseModel):
    fields: list[FieldSpec] = Field(description="Non-empty list of field definitions")


class FieldInfo(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    name: str
    type: str
    nullable: bool


class SchemaVersion(BaseModel):
    dataset_id: int
    dataset_name: str
    version: int
    created_at: str
    fields: list[FieldInfo]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Read-only schema version diff
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class FieldChangeDefinition(BaseModel):
    type: str
    nullable: bool


class VersionFieldChange(BaseModel):
    field: str
    kind: Literal["added", "removed", "changed"]
    # Null on the side where the field does not exist; never omitted.
    before: FieldChangeDefinition | None
    after: FieldChangeDefinition | None


class VersionDiffResponse(BaseModel):
    from_version: int
    to_version: int
    compatible: bool
    changes: list[VersionFieldChange]


class LineageCreate(BaseModel):
    target_dataset: str
    target_version: int
    target_field: str
    source_dataset: str
    source_version: int
    source_field: str


class LineageSourceRef(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    field: str


class TargetFieldLineage(BaseModel):
    target_field: str
    sources: list[LineageSourceRef]


class LineageCreatedResponse(BaseModel):
    target_dataset: str
    target_version: int
    target_field: str
    source: LineageSourceRef


class LineageResponse(BaseModel):
    target_dataset: str
    target_version: int
    fields: list[TargetFieldLineage]


class LineageImpactResponse(BaseModel):
    source: LineageSourceRef
    impacted: list[LineageSourceRef]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Quality rules
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


QualityRuleKind = Literal["not_null", "numeric_range", "unique"]


class QualityRuleCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    name: str = Field(description="Unique rule name within the version")
    kind: QualityRuleKind
    params: dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Kind-specific parameters: {'field': ...}, "
        "{'field': ..., 'min': ..., 'max': ...} or {'fields': [...]}",
    )


class QualityRule(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    kind: QualityRuleKind
    params: dict[str, Any]
    enabled: bool
    created_at: str


class QualityRuleEnabledUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    enabled: StrictBool


class QualityRuleEvaluateRequest(BaseModel):
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        description="Rows to check; only enabled rules are executed"
    )


class QualityRuleResult(BaseModel):
    rule_id: int
    name: str
    passed: bool
    violations: list[int]


class QualityRuleEvaluateResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    results: list[QualityRuleResult]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Quality rule evaluation history and diff
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class QualityRuleEvaluationRecord(BaseModel):
    sequence: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    row_count: int
    violation_row_count: int
    results: list[QualityRuleResult]
    created_at: str


class QualityRuleEvaluationSide(BaseModel):
    violation_count: int
    violations: list[int]


class QualityRuleEvaluationRuleDiff(BaseModel):
    rule_id: int
    name: str
    # Null on the side whose evaluation has no result for this rule (e.g. the
    # rule was disabled or did not exist yet); never omitted.
    before: QualityRuleEvaluationSide | None
    after: QualityRuleEvaluationSide | None
    # Null exactly when a side is missing: a row-level diff needs both sides.
    added_violations: list[int] | None
    removed_violations: list[int] | None
    violation_count_delta: int | None


class QualityRuleEvaluationDiffResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    # Null (with empty lists) when fewer than two evaluations are recorded.
    from_sequence: int | None
    to_sequence: int | None
    added_violation_rows: list[int]
    removed_violation_rows: list[int]
    rules: list[QualityRuleEvaluationRuleDiff]


class ErrorResponse(BaseModel):
    error: str
    detail: str | None = None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Privacy policies
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


PrivacyMasking = Literal["redact", "partial"]


class PrivacyPolicyCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    field: StrictStr = Field(description="Existing field of the schema version")
    classification: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty sensitivity classification")
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    allowed_roles: list[StrictStr] = Field(
        description="Distinct, non-empty role names that see the raw value; may be empty"
    )


class PrivacyPolicy(BaseModel):
    id: int
    field: str
    classification: str
    masking: PrivacyMasking
    allowed_roles: list[str]
    enabled: bool
    created_at: str


class PrivacyPolicyEnabledUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    enabled: StrictBool


class PrivacyViewRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    role: StrictStr
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]]


class PrivacyViewResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Row snapshots
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class SnapshotCreate(BaseModel):
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(
        description="Row objects to persist; values and order are stored verbatim"
    )


class SnapshotMetadata(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    created_at: str
    row_count: int


class SnapshotResponse(SnapshotMetadata):
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]]


class SnapshotDiffEntry(BaseModel):
    row: dict[str, Any]
    count: int


class SnapshotDiffResponse(BaseModel):
    from_snapshot_id: int
    to_snapshot_id: int
    added: list[SnapshotDiffEntry]
    removed: list[SnapshotDiffEntry]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Retention policies and lineage-aware snapshot deletion
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class RetentionPolicyCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    retention_days: StrictInt = Field(
        ge=0, description="Non-negative minimum snapshot age in days"
    )


class RetentionPolicy(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    retention_days: int
    created_at: str


class SnapshotDeletionRequestCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    reason: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty reason for the requested deletion")


class SnapshotDeletionRequest(BaseModel):
    id: int
    snapshot_id: int
    policy_id: int
    reason: str
    status: Literal["pending", "blocked", "confirmed"]
    impacted: list[LineageSourceRef]
    created_at: str


class ConfirmedSnapshotDeletionRequest(SnapshotDeletionRequest):
    confirmed_at: str


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Retention exceptions (compliance holds blocking snapshot deletion)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


RetentionExceptionScope = Literal["version", "snapshot"]


class RetentionExceptionCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    scope: RetentionExceptionScope
    snapshot_id: StrictInt | None = Field(
        description="Null for scope 'version'; an existing snapshot id of this "
        "version for scope 'snapshot'"
    )
    reason: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty justification for the hold")
    expires_at: StrictStr = Field(
        description="Future ISO-8601 date-time including a timezone"
    )


class RetentionException(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    scope: RetentionExceptionScope
    snapshot_id: int | None
    reason: str
    expires_at: str
    status: Literal["active", "expired", "released"]
    created_at: str
    released_at: str | None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Processing tasks
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class ProcessingTaskCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    name: StrictStr = Field(description="Unique, non-empty task name within the version")
    depends_on: list[StrictInt] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Ids of tasks in the same version that must succeed first",
    )
    max_attempts: StrictInt = Field(
        default=1, ge=1, description="Maximum number of runs allowed for the task"
    )


class ProcessingTask(BaseModel):
    id: int
    dataset: str
    version: int
    name: str
    depends_on: list[int]
    max_attempts: int
    status: Literal["pending", "running", "succeeded", "failed"]
    attempt_count: int
    created_at: str


class ProcessingTaskRun(BaseModel):
    id: int
    task_id: int
    attempt: int
    status: Literal["running", "succeeded", "failed"]
    started_at: str
    finished_at: str | None
    error: str | None


class ProcessingTaskWithRuns(ProcessingTask):
    runs: list[ProcessingTaskRun]


class ProcessingRunFinish(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    status: Literal["succeeded", "failed"]
    error: StrictStr | None = None


class ProcessingRunCancel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    reason: StrictStr = Field(
        description="Non-empty reason for cancelling the run; trimmed before storing"
    )


class ProcessingTaskDispatchRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    # Non-optional with a default: omission yields 1, while an explicit null is
    # rejected like any other non-integer ("given" values must be positive ints).
    limit: StrictInt = Field(
        default=1,
        ge=1,
        description="Maximum number of tasks to start; defaults to 1 when omitted",
    )


class ProcessingTaskDispatchResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    runs: list[ProcessingTaskRun]


# Sentinel default for ProcessingRunBatchCompleteItem.error: unlike the
# single-run finish payload, the batch item must distinguish an omitted error
# field from an explicitly supplied one, because a success item may only omit
# the field — writing it at all (even as null) is a 422.
ERROR_FIELD_UNSET: Any = object()


class ProcessingRunBatchCompleteItem(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    task_id: StrictInt
    run_id: StrictInt
    status: Literal["succeeded", "failed"]
    # Omitted for success, a non-empty message for failure. An explicitly
    # supplied value (null included) stays distinguishable from omission via
    # the sentinel default; the success/failure rules are enforced in the
    # repository after the path resolves so 404 precedence is preserved.
    error: StrictStr | None = ERROR_FIELD_UNSET


class ProcessingRunBatchCompleteRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    runs: list[ProcessingRunBatchCompleteItem] = Field(
        min_length=1,
        description="Non-empty batch of task/run completions for the path version",
    )


class ProcessingRunBatchCompleteResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    runs: list[ProcessingTaskRun]


class ProcessingTaskDependenciesUpdate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    depends_on: list[StrictInt] = Field(
        description="Replacement list of ids of tasks in the same version; may be empty"
    )


ScheduleState = Literal[
    "running", "succeeded", "retryable", "exhausted", "ready", "blocked",
    "upstream_failed",
]


class ScheduledTask(ProcessingTask):
    schedule_state: ScheduleState
    blocking_task_ids: list[int]


class ProcessingScheduleResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    tasks: list[ScheduledTask]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Processing task run audit records
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class AuditRecordCreate(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    event: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty name of the audited event")
    input_summary: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty summary of the input")
    result_summary: StrictStr = Field(description="Non-empty summary of the result")


class AuditRecord(BaseModel):
    id: int
    sequence: int
    event: str
    input_summary: str
    result_summary: str
    run_status: Literal["running", "succeeded", "failed"]
    previous_hash: str | None
    evidence_hash: str
    created_at: str


class AuditChainVerifyResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    task_id: int
    run_id: int
    valid: bool
    checked_count: int


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Read-only per-version processing audit report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class AuditChainProof(BaseModel):
    valid: bool
    checked_count: int
    # Stored evidence hash of the chain's final record; null only when the
    # chain is empty (it is still reported when valid is false).
    last_evidence_hash: str | None


class AuditReportRun(ProcessingTaskRun):
    proof: AuditChainProof


class AuditReportTask(ProcessingTask):
    runs: list[AuditReportRun]


class ProcessingAuditReportSummary(BaseModel):
    task_count: int
    run_count: int
    pending_tasks: int
    running_tasks: int
    succeeded_tasks: int
    failed_tasks: int
    # Subset of failed_tasks whose attempt budget is used up.
    exhausted_tasks: int
    # Runs whose audit chain failed re-verification.
    invalid_audit_runs: int


class ProcessingAuditReportResponse(BaseModel):
    dataset: str
    version: int
    summary: ProcessingAuditReportSummary
    tasks: list[AuditReportTask]

73	    )

76	@app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
77	def handle_validation_error(
78	    request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError
79	) -> JSONResponse:
80	    missing: list[str] = []
81	    invalid: list[str] = []
82	    malformed_json = False
83	    for error in exc.errors():
84	        if error.get("type") in ("json_invalid", "json_decode"):
85	            malformed_json = True
86	            continue
87	        loc = [str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()) if part != "body"]
88	        path = ".".join(loc)
89	        if error.get("type") == "missing":
90	            missing.append(path or "body")
91	        else:
92	            invalid.append(path or "body")
93	    if malformed_json and not missing and not invalid:
94	        message = "Request body is not valid JSON"
95	    elif missing:
96	        message = (
97	            "Request body is incomplete: missing field(s) "
98	            + ", ".join(sorted(set(missing)))
99	        )
100	    elif invalid:
101	        message = (
102	            "The request payload is invalid for field(s) "
103	            + ", ".join(sorted(set(invalid)))
104	        )
105	    else:
106	        message = "The request payload is invalid"
107	    return JSONResponse(
108	        status_code=422,

110	    )

204	def diff_schema_versions(
205	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
206	    dataset_name: str,
207	    from_version: int,
208	    to_version: int,
209	    *,
210	    body: bytes = b"",
211	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
212	) -> dict:
213	    """Read-only diff of the persisted field definitions of two versions.
214	
215	    ``from`` is the baseline and ``to`` the target. Only the stored field
216	    definitions (name, type, nullable) are compared; field position is not a
217	    difference. Changes are sorted by field name and each carries ``before``
218	    and ``after`` definitions, null on the side where the field does not
219	    exist. ``compatible`` reports whether the target can take over the
220	    baseline's fields: a removal, a type change or a nullable tightening
221	    (nullable -> not nullable) makes it false; additions and nullable
222	    loosening keep it true.
223	
224	    The endpoint takes no parameters: a non-positive version number is a 422
225	    checked before path resolution, while a non-empty request body or any
226	    query parameter is a 422 raised only after the path dataset and both
227	    versions have resolved, so an unknown dataset/version stays a 404
228	    (mirroring the parameterless audit-report endpoint). Nothing is written.
229	    """
230	    if from_version < 1 or to_version < 1:
231	        raise RequestInvalidError(
232	            "Version numbers in the diff path must be positive integers"
233	        )
234	
235	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
236	    from_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, from_version)
237	    to_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, to_version)
238	
239	    if body.strip():
240	        raise RequestInvalidError(
241	            "The version diff endpoint does not accept a request body"
242	        )
243	    if query_keys:
244	        raise RequestInvalidError(
245	            "The version diff endpoint does not accept query parameters"
246	        )
247	
248	    from_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, from_row["id"])
249	    to_fields = _version_field_definitions(conn, to_row["id"])
250	
251	    changes: list[dict] = []
252	    compatible = True
253	    for name in sorted(set(from_fields) | set(to_fields)):
254	        before = from_fields.get(name)
255	        after = to_fields.get(name)
256	        if before == after:
257	            continue
258	        if before is None:
259	            changes.append(
260	                {"field": name, "kind": "added", "before": None, "after": after}
261	            )
262	        elif after is None:
263	            changes.append(
264	                {"field": name, "kind": "removed", "before": before, "after": None}
265	            )
266	            compatible = False
267	        else:
268	            changes.append(
269	                {"field": name, "kind": "changed", "before": before, "after": after}
270	            )
271	            if before["type"] != after["type"] or (
272	                before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]
273	            ):
274	                compatible = False
275	
276	    return {
277	        "from_version": from_row["version"],
278	        "to_version": to_row["version"],
279	        "compatible": compatible,
280	        "changes": changes,
281	    }

449	def _lineage_forward_edges(
450	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
451	) -> dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]]:
452	    """Adjacency of the lineage graph: source field id -> target field refs."""
453	    rows = conn.execute(
454	        """
455	        SELECT  ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
456	                ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
457	                td.name            AS target_dataset,
458	                tv.version         AS target_version,
459	                tf.name            AS target_field
460	        FROM    lineage_links ll
461	        JOIN    datasets td ON td.id = ll.target_dataset_id
462	        JOIN    schema_versions tv ON tv.id = ll.target_version_id
463	        JOIN    schema_fields tf ON tf.id = ll.target_field_id
464	        """
465	    ).fetchall()
466	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]] = {}
467	    for row in rows:
468	        ref = {
469	            "dataset": row["target_dataset"],
470	            "version": row["target_version"],
471	            "field": row["target_field"],
472	        }
473	        edges.setdefault(row["source_field_id"], []).append(
474	            (row["target_field_id"], ref)
475	        )
476	    return edges

479	def _compute_impacted(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source_field_id: int) -> list[dict]:
480	    """All fields reachable downstream of the source, deduplicated and sorted.
481	
482	    The source field id is seeded into the visited set, so cycles terminate
483	    and the source itself never appears in the result.
484	    """
485	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
486	    visited = {source_field_id}
487	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
488	    queue = [source_field_id]
489	    while queue:
490	        current = queue.pop()
491	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
492	            if target_field_id in visited:
493	                continue
494	            visited.add(target_field_id)
495	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
496	            queue.append(target_field_id)
497	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]

505	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
506	        (dataset, version, field),

517	) -> None:

520	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
521	        (dataset, version, field),
522	    )

524	        "INSERT INTO lineage_impact_cache ("
525	        "source_dataset, source_version, source_field, impacted, created_at"
526	        ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
527	        (dataset, version, field, json.dumps(impacted), utc_now_iso()),
528	    )
529	    cache_id = cursor.lastrowid
530	    mentioned = {dataset} | {item["dataset"] for item in impacted}
531	    conn.executemany(
532	        "INSERT INTO lineage_impact_cache_datasets (cache_id, dataset) "
533	        "VALUES (?, ?)",

535	    )

540	) -> None:

545	        ")",

550	def _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
551	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
552	    source_dataset: str,
553	    source_version: int,
554	    source_field: str,
555	    source_field_id: int,
556	) -> None:
557	    """Invalidate cached impacts of the new link's source and its upstream.
558	
559	    A new mapping ``source -> target`` only changes the impact result of
560	    fields that can reach ``source`` (``source`` itself included), so exactly
561	    those cached entries are dropped; unrelated entries are kept. The reverse
562	    walk runs after the link was inserted so cycles are covered too.
563	    """
564	    rows = conn.execute(
565	        """
566	        SELECT  ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
567	                ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
568	                sd.name            AS source_dataset,
569	                sv.version         AS source_version,
570	                sf.name            AS source_field
571	        FROM    lineage_links ll
572	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id
573	        JOIN    schema_versions sv ON sv.id = ll.source_version_id
574	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
575	        """
576	    ).fetchall()
577	    reverse: dict[int, list[sqlite3.Row]] = {}
578	    for row in rows:
579	        reverse.setdefault(row["target_field_id"], []).append(row)
580	
581	    visited = {source_field_id}
582	    upstream = {(source_dataset, source_version, source_field)}
583	    queue = [source_field_id]
584	    while queue:
585	        current = queue.pop()
586	        for row in reverse.get(current, ()):
587	            if row["source_field_id"] in visited:
588	                continue
589	            visited.add(row["source_field_id"])
590	            upstream.add(
591	                (row["source_dataset"], row["source_version"], row["source_field"])
592	            )
593	            queue.append(row["source_field_id"])
594	
595	    conn.executemany(
596	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
597	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
598	        sorted(upstream),
599	    )

649	def _is_finite_number(value: Any) -> bool:
650	    # bool is a subclass of int; a boolean is not a numeric value here.
651	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
652	        return False

656	def _validate_rule_params(
657	    kind: str, params: dict[str, Any], field_names: set[str]
658	) -> None:
659	    """Validate rule parameters structurally (422) and against the schema (404)."""
660	
661	    def require_existing_field(field_name: Any) -> str:
662	        if not isinstance(field_name, str) or not field_name:
663	            raise RequestInvalidError(
664	                f"Rule kind '{kind}' requires a non-empty 'field' parameter"
665	            )
666	        if field_name not in field_names:
667	            raise NotFoundError(f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in this version")
668	        return field_name
669	
670	    if kind == "not_null":
671	        require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
672	        return
673	
674	    if kind == "numeric_range":
675	        field_name = require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
676	        minimum = params.get("min")
677	        maximum = params.get("max")
678	        if not _is_finite_number(minimum) or not _is_finite_number(maximum):
679	            raise RequestInvalidError(
680	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires finite numeric 'min' and 'max'"
681	            )
682	        if minimum > maximum:
683	            raise RequestInvalidError(
684	                f"Rule on field '{field_name}' requires min <= max"
685	            )
686	        return
687	
688	    if kind == "unique":
689	        fields = params.get("fields")
690	        if not isinstance(fields, list) or not fields:
691	            raise RequestInvalidError(
692	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires a non-empty 'fields' list"
693	            )
694	        if not all(isinstance(name, str) and name for name in fields):
695	            raise RequestInvalidError(
696	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain non-empty field names"
697	            )
698	        if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
699	            raise RequestInvalidError(
700	                "Rule kind 'unique' requires 'fields' to contain no duplicates"
701	            )
702	        unknown = [name for name in fields if name not in field_names]
703	        if unknown:
704	            raise NotFoundError(
705	                f"Field '{unknown[0]}' does not exist in this version"
706	            )
707	        return

830	    # JSON text so that, e.g., the number 1 and the string "1" never compare
831	    # equal and nested objects with reordered keys still match.
832	    return json.dumps(combo, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))

835	def evaluate_quality_rules(
836	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int, rows: list[dict]
837	) -> dict:
838	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
839	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
840	
841	    rule_rows = conn.execute(
842	        "SELECT id, name, kind, params, enabled "
843	        "FROM quality_rules WHERE version_id = ? AND enabled = 1 ORDER BY id",
844	        (version_row["id"],),
845	    ).fetchall()
846	
847	    results: list[dict] = []
848	    for rule_row in rule_rows:
849	        params = json.loads(rule_row["params"])
850	        kind = rule_row["kind"]
851	        violations: list[int] = []
852	
853	        if kind == "not_null":
854	            field = params["field"]
855	            violations = [
856	                index
857	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
858	                if _row_violates_not_null(row, field)
859	            ]
860	        elif kind == "numeric_range":
861	            field = params["field"]
862	            violations = [
863	                index
864	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
865	                if _row_violates_numeric_range(
866	                    row, field, params["min"], params["max"]
867	                )
868	            ]
869	        elif kind == "unique":
870	            fields = params["fields"]
871	            seen: dict[str, int] = {}
872	            duplicated: set[int] = set()
873	            for index, row in enumerate(rows):
874	                combo = _row_violates_unique(row, fields)
875	                key = _json_combo_key(combo)
876	                if key in seen:
877	                    duplicated.add(seen[key])
878	                    duplicated.add(index)
879	                else:
880	                    seen[key] = index
881	            violations = sorted(duplicated)
882	
883	        results.append(
884	            {
885	                "rule_id": rule_row["id"],
886	                "name": rule_row["name"],
887	                "passed": not violations,
888	                "violations": violations,
889	            }
890	        )
891	
892	    # Every successful evaluation appends an immutable summary to the history
893	    # (an empty submission is recorded too, with zero violations). A rejected
894	    # or failed evaluation raises above and leaves no record.
895	    _record_quality_rule_evaluation(
896	        conn,
897	        version_row["id"],
898	        row_count=len(rows),
899	        violation_row_count=len(
900	            {index for result in results for index in result["violations"]}
901	        ),
902	        results=results,
903	    )
904	
905	    return {
906	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
907	        "version": version_row["version"],
908	        "results": results,
909	    }

912	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
913	# Quality rule evaluation history (append-only) and read-only diff
914	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
915	
916	
917	# Serializes read-tail -> append within this process so concurrent evaluations
918	# never compute the same sequence. SQLite's UNIQUE(version_id, sequence)
919	# constraint is the hard guard against writers in other processes; such a
920	# collision is resolved with a bounded re-read-and-retry (mirrors the audit
921	# record append).
922	_evaluation_append_locks: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}
923	_evaluation_append_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
924	
925	# Bound on re-read-and-retry attempts when a writer in another process wins the
926	# race for the same (version_id, sequence).
927	_EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 100
928	
929	
930	def _evaluation_append_lock(version_id: int) -> threading.Lock:
931	    with _evaluation_append_locks_guard:
932	        lock = _evaluation_append_locks.get(version_id)
933	        if lock is None:
934	            lock = threading.Lock()
935	            _evaluation_append_locks[version_id] = lock
936	        return lock
937	
938	
939	def _record_quality_rule_evaluation(
940	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
941	    version_id: int,
942	    *,
943	    row_count: int,
944	    violation_row_count: int,
945	    results: list[dict],
946	) -> None:
947	    """Append one evaluation summary as the next sequence of the version.
948	
949	    The per-version lock makes read-tail -> append atomic within this process
950	    (FastAPI runs this synchronous endpoint in one process's threadpool). The
951	    UNIQUE(version_id, sequence) constraint is the hard cross-process guard; a
952	    writer that loses a race against another process retries with the new tail
953	    instead of failing the request.
954	    """
955	    stored_results = json.dumps(results)
956	    with _evaluation_append_lock(version_id):
957	        for attempt in range(_EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
958	            tail = conn.execute(
959	                "SELECT MAX(sequence) AS max_sequence "
960	                "FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ?",
961	                (version_id,),
962	            ).fetchone()
963	            sequence = (tail["max_sequence"] or 0) + 1
964	            try:
965	                conn.execute(
966	                    "INSERT INTO quality_rule_evaluations ("
967	                    "version_id, sequence, row_count, violation_row_count, "
968	                    "results, created_at"
969	                    ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
970	                    (
971	                        version_id,
972	                        sequence,
973	                        row_count,
974	                        violation_row_count,
975	                        stored_results,
976	                        utc_now_iso(),
977	                    ),
978	                )
979	                return
980	            except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
981	                # Another process inserted the same sequence first. End the
982	                # current (pinned) transaction so the re-read establishes a new
983	                # snapshot that includes the competing commit, then retry.
984	                if attempt + 1 == _EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
985	                    conn.rollback()
986	                    raise ConflictError(
987	                        "Too many concurrent evaluation writes; retry the request"
988	                    )
989	                conn.rollback()
990	                continue
991

1059	def diff_quality_rule_evaluations(
1060	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1061	    dataset_name: str,
1062	    version_number: int,
1063	    *,
1064	    body: bytes = b"",
1065	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
1066	) -> dict:
1067	    """Read-only diff between the two most recent evaluations of one version.
1068	
1069	    The latest recorded evaluation (``to``) is compared against its immediate
1070	    predecessor (``from``) using exactly the results each of them recorded;
1071	    the persisted rule definitions and submitted rows of the two evaluations
1072	    are all that is consulted. Row positions are the 0-based indices each
1073	    evaluation reported. A rule missing from one side (disabled or not yet
1074	    created between the two evaluations) keeps a null side, and its row-level
1075	    diff fields are null as well, so a missing side stays distinguishable from
1076	    a present side with zero violations. With fewer than two recorded
1077	    evaluations the result is explicitly empty (null sequences, empty lists),
1078	    never an error. Nothing is written.
1079	    """
1080	    dataset, version_row = _require_evaluation_path(
1081	        conn, dataset_name, version_number, body=body, query_keys=query_keys,
1082	        endpoint="evaluation diff",
1083	    )
1084	    rows = conn.execute(
1085	        "SELECT * FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ? "
1086	        "ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 2",
1087	        (version_row["id"],),
1088	    ).fetchall()
1089	
1090	    empty = {
1091	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1092	        "version": version_row["version"],
1093	        "from_sequence": None,
1094	        "to_sequence": None,
1095	        "added_violation_rows": [],
1096	        "removed_violation_rows": [],
1097	        "rules": [],
1098	    }
1099	    if len(rows) < 2:
1100	        return empty
1101	
1102	    to_row, from_row = rows[0], rows[1]
1103	    before_results = {r["rule_id"]: r for r in json.loads(from_row["results"])}
1104	    after_results = {r["rule_id"]: r for r in json.loads(to_row["results"])}
1105	
1106	    rule_diffs: list[dict] = []
1107	    for rule_id in sorted(set(before_results) | set(after_results)):
1108	        before = before_results.get(rule_id)
1109	        after = after_results.get(rule_id)
1110	        if before is not None and after is not None:
1111	            before_set = set(before["violations"])
1112	            after_set = set(after["violations"])
1113	            added: list[int] | None = sorted(after_set - before_set)
1114	            removed: list[int] | None = sorted(before_set - after_set)
1115	            delta: int | None = len(after["violations"]) - len(before["violations"])
1116	        else:
1117	            added = removed = delta = None
1118	        rule_diffs.append(
1119	            {
1120	                "rule_id": rule_id,
1121	                "name": (after if after is not None else before)["name"],
1122	                "before": (
1123	                    None
1124	                    if before is None
1125	                    else {
1126	                        "violation_count": len(before["violations"]),
1127	                        "violations": before["violations"],
1128	                    }
1129	                ),
1130	                "after": (
1131	                    None
1132	                    if after is None
1133	                    else {
1134	                        "violation_count": len(after["violations"]),
1135	                        "violations": after["violations"],
1136	                    }
1137	                ),
1138	                "added_violations": added,
1139	                "removed_violations": removed,
1140	                "violation_count_delta": delta,
1141	            }
1142	        )
1143	
1144	    before_rows = {
1145	        index for result in before_results.values() for index in result["violations"]
1146	    }
1147	    after_rows = {
1148	        index for result in after_results.values() for index in result["violations"]
1149	    }
1150	
1151	    return {
1152	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1153	        "version": version_row["version"],
1154	        "from_sequence": from_row["sequence"],
1155	        "to_sequence": to_row["sequence"],
1156	        "added_violation_rows": sorted(after_rows - before_rows),
1157	        "removed_violation_rows": sorted(before_rows - after_rows),
1158	        "rules": rule_diffs,
1159	    }

1434	def _parse_at_timestamp(raw: str) -> datetime:
1435	    try:
1436	        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
1437	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
1438	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1439	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
1440	        ) from exc
1441	    # A trailing timezone designator (offset or 'Z') is mandatory.
1442	    if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() is None:
1443	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1444	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' must include a timezone"
1445	        )
1446	    return parsed

1449	def get_snapshot_at(
1450	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1451	    dataset_name: str,
1452	    version_number: int,
1453	    raw_timestamp: str | None,
1454	) -> dict:
1455	    if raw_timestamp is None or not raw_timestamp:
1456	        raise RequestInvalidError(
1457	            "Query parameter 'timestamp' is required and must be an ISO-8601 date-time"
1458	        )
1459	    target = _parse_at_timestamp(raw_timestamp)
1460	
1461	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1462	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1463	
1464	    # Select the newest snapshot chronologically (ties broken by the highest
1465	    # id); comparing parsed instants also handles any offset in the target.
1466	    candidates = conn.execute(
1467	        "SELECT id, created_at FROM snapshots WHERE version_id = ?",
1468	        (version_row["id"],),
1469	    ).fetchall()
1470	    eligible = [
1471	        (datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]), row["id"])
1472	        for row in candidates
1473	        if datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]) <= target
1474	    ]
1475	    if not eligible:
1476	        raise NotFoundError(
1477	            f"No snapshot of version {version_number} of dataset "
1478	            f"'{dataset_name}' exists at or before the requested timestamp"
1479	        )
1480	    match_id = max(eligible, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1]))[1]
1481	
1482	    row = conn.execute(
1483	        "SELECT id, row_count, rows, created_at FROM snapshots WHERE id = ?",
1484	        (match_id,),
1485	    ).fetchone()
1486	    result = _snapshot_metadata(row, dataset["name"], version_row["version"])
1487	    result["rows"] = json.loads(row["rows"])
1488	    return result

1508	def _canonical_row_text(row: Any) -> str:
1509	    # Object key order is ignored (sort_keys) while array order and value types
1510	    # are preserved (e.g. 1 vs "1" vs 1.0 vs true all differ).
1511	    return json.dumps(row, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)

1514	def _snapshot_multiset(
1515	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
1516	) -> tuple[Counter, dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
1517	    counts: Counter = Counter()
1518	    examples: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
1519	    for row in rows:
1520	        key = _canonical_row_text(row)
1521	        counts[key] += 1
1522	        examples.setdefault(key, row)
1523	    return counts, examples

1526	def diff_snapshots(
1527	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1528	    dataset_name: str,
1529	    version_number: int,
1530	    from_snapshot_id: int,
1531	    to_snapshot_id: int,
1532	) -> dict:
1533	    # Validate the path target first so unknown dataset/version stay 404.
1534	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1535	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1536	
1537	    from_row = _find_snapshot_globally(conn, from_snapshot_id)
1538	    if from_row is None:
1539	        raise NotFoundError(f"Snapshot {from_snapshot_id} does not exist")
1540	    to_row = _find_snapshot_globally(conn, to_snapshot_id)
1541	    if to_row is None:
1542	        raise NotFoundError(f"Snapshot {to_snapshot_id} does not exist")
1543	
1544	    for row, snapshot_id in ((from_row, from_snapshot_id), (to_row, to_snapshot_id)):
1545	        if row["version_id"] != version_row["id"]:
1546	            raise RequestInvalidError(
1547	                f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not belong to version "
1548	                f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'; snapshots can "
1549	                "only be compared within the same dataset and version"
1550	            )
1551	
1552	    from_rows = json.loads(from_row["rows"])
1553	    to_rows = json.loads(to_row["rows"])
1554	    from_counts, from_examples = _snapshot_multiset(from_rows)
1555	    to_counts, to_examples = _snapshot_multiset(to_rows)
1556	
1557	    added_keys = sorted(key for key in to_counts if to_counts[key] > from_counts[key])
1558	    removed_keys = sorted(key for key in from_counts if from_counts[key] > to_counts[key])
1559	
1560	    return {
1561	        "from_snapshot_id": from_snapshot_id,
1562	        "to_snapshot_id": to_snapshot_id,
1563	        "added": [
1564	            {"row": to_examples[key], "count": to_counts[key] - from_counts[key]}
1565	            for key in added_keys
1566	        ],
1567	        "removed": [
1568	            {"row": from_examples[key], "count": from_counts[key] - to_counts[key]}
1569	            for key in removed_keys
1570	        ],
1571	    }

1619	def _compute_version_field_impacted(
1620	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, version_id: int
1621	) -> list[dict]:
1622	    """Downstream union of every field of one schema version.
1623	
1624	    All of the version's fields seed the same reachability walk, so direct and
1625	    indirect downstream fields are found once, cycles terminate and the version's
1626	    own fields never appear in the result.
1627	    """
1628	    field_rows = conn.execute(
1629	        "SELECT id FROM schema_fields WHERE version_id = ?", (version_id,)
1630	    ).fetchall()
1631	    seeds = [row["id"] for row in field_rows]
1632	
1633	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
1634	    visited = set(seeds)
1635	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
1636	    queue = list(seeds)
1637	    while queue:
1638	        current = queue.pop()
1639	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
1640	            if target_field_id in visited:
1641	                continue
1642	            visited.add(target_field_id)
1643	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
1644	            queue.append(target_field_id)
1645	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]

1660	def create_snapshot_deletion_request(
1661	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1662	    dataset_name: str,
1663	    version_number: int,
1664	    snapshot_id: int,
1665	    reason: str,
1666	) -> dict:
1667	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1668	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1669	
1670	    clean_reason = reason.strip()
1671	    if not clean_reason:
1672	        raise RequestInvalidError("'reason' must not be empty")
1673	
1674	    snapshot_row = _get_scoped_snapshot_row(conn, version_row["id"], snapshot_id)
1675	    if snapshot_row is None:
1676	        raise NotFoundError(
1677	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not exist in version "
1678	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1679	        )
1680	
1681	    policy_row = conn.execute(
1682	        "SELECT id FROM retention_policies WHERE version_id = ?",
1683	        (version_row["id"],),
1684	    ).fetchone()
1685	    if policy_row is None:
1686	        raise NotFoundError(
1687	            f"No retention policy exists for version {version_number} of "
1688	            f"dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1689	        )
1690	
1691	    open_request = conn.execute(
1692	        "SELECT id FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "
1693	        "WHERE snapshot_id = ? AND status IN ('pending', 'blocked')",
1694	        (snapshot_id,),
1695	    ).fetchone()
1696	    if open_request is not None:
1697	        raise ConflictError(
1698	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} already has an open deletion request "
1699	            f"({open_request['id']})"
1700	        )
1701	
1702	    # An active retention exception (version- or snapshot-scoped) forbids
1703	    # opening a deletion request; the check shares this transaction with the
1704	    # insert below, so the two commit atomically.
1705	    _require_no_active_retention_exception(
1706	        conn, version_row, snapshot_id, dataset_name, version_number
1707	    )
1708	
1709	    impacted = _compute_version_field_impacted(conn, version_row["id"])
1710	    status = "blocked" if impacted else "pending"
1711	    try:
1712	        cursor = conn.execute(
1713	            "INSERT INTO snapshot_deletion_requests ("
1714	            "version_id, snapshot_id, policy_id, reason, status, impacted, created_at"
1715	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
1716	            (
1717	                version_row["id"],
1718	                snapshot_id,
1719	                policy_row["id"],
1720	                clean_reason,
1721	                status,
1722	                json.dumps(impacted),
1723	                utc_now_iso(),
1724	            ),
1725	        )
1726	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
1727	        # Lost a race against a concurrent open-request insert.
1728	        raise ConflictError(
1729	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} already has an open deletion request"
1730	        ) from exc
1731	    row = conn.execute(
1732	        "SELECT * FROM snapshot_deletion_requests WHERE id = ?",
1733	        (cursor.lastrowid,),
1734	    ).fetchone()
1735	    return _deletion_request_row_to_dict(row)
1736

1738	def list_snapshot_deletion_requests(

1746

1748	    # away: the snapshot itself may be gone, but its request records remain.
1749	    # A snapshot id that never existed in this version and has no requests is an
1750	    # unknown resource.
1751	    snapshot_row = _get_scoped_snapshot_row(conn, version_row["id"], snapshot_id)
1752	    request_rows = conn.execute(

1759	            f"Snapshot {snapshot_id} does not exist in version "
1760	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
1761	        )
1762

1764	        "SELECT * FROM snapshot_deletion_requests "
1765	        "WHERE version_id = ? AND snapshot_id = ? ORDER BY id",

def database_path() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("DATA_LINEAGE_DB", DEFAULT_DB_PATH))


def _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = database_path()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    # Schema creation is idempotent and committed independently, so every
    # request works against an initialized database file.
    for statement in SCHEMA_STATEMENTS:
        conn.execute(statement)
    conn.commit()
    return conn


@contextmanager
def db_session() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    conn = _connect()
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except BaseException:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


def get_db() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    """FastAPI dependency yielding a transactional database connection."""
    with db_session() as conn:
        yield conn

2532	def batch_complete_task_runs(
2533	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
2534	    dataset_name: str,
2535	    version_number: int,
2536	    items: list[dict[str, Any]],
2537	    *,
2538	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
2539	) -> dict:
2540	    """Finish a non-empty batch of currently running runs in one transaction.
2541	
2542	    Every item names a task of the path version together with one of its runs
2543	    and declares ``succeeded`` (the error field must be omitted altogether;
2544	    an explicit value, including null, is rejected) or ``failed`` (an error
2545	    that is non-empty after trimming). The whole batch is validated before any
2546	    write: the path dataset/version must exist (404); query parameters are
2547	    rejected (422); per-item status/error rules are checked (422); every named
2548	    task must exist in the version (404) and must not appear twice (409); every
2549	    run must exist (404), belong to the named task when it is in the same
2550	    version (422) and still be ``running`` with its task currently completable
2551	    (409). A run owned by a task in another dataset/version is treated as not
2552	    existing in this version (404).
2553	
2554	    On success every run gets a ``finished_at`` timestamp and its terminal
2555	    status, and the owning task moves to the same status atomically; the result
2556	    runs are returned ordered by task id ascending. A ``failed`` task keeps its
2557	    ``attempt_count`` and follows the existing retry rules. The process lock
2558	    and ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` serialize against single finish/cancel/start and
2559	    dispatch; the conditional ``UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'running'`` is the
2560	    hard single-winner guard, so any racing request gets a 409 with the whole
2561	    batch rolled back and no half-written row.
2562	    """
2563	    with _processing_write_section():
2564	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
2565	        try:
2566	            dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
2567	            version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
2568	
2569	            if query_keys:
2570	                raise RequestInvalidError(
2571	                    "The batch-complete endpoint does not accept query parameters"
2572	                )
2573	
2574	            # Phase 1: resolve every named task within the path version. All
2575	            # existence checks precede every other per-item check so an unknown
2576	            # task stays a 404 regardless of the batch order or any other
2577	            # invalid item.
2578	            task_rows: dict[int, sqlite3.Row] = {}
2579	            for item in items:
2580	                task_id = item["task_id"]
2581	                task_row = conn.execute(
2582	                    "SELECT * FROM processing_tasks WHERE version_id = ? AND id = ?",
2583	                    (version_row["id"], task_id),
2584	                ).fetchone()
2585	                if task_row is None:
2586	                    raise NotFoundError(
2587	                        f"Processing task {task_id} does not exist in version "
2588	                        f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
2589	                    )
2590	                task_rows[task_id] = task_row
2591	
2592	            # Phase 2: per-item payload semantics, mirroring the single finish
2593	            # endpoint (which resolves the path task before these same checks):
2594	            # a success may only omit the error field — writing it explicitly
2595	            # in any form, including null, is rejected — and a failure needs a
2596	            # non-blank error string.
2597	            for item in items:
2598	                status = item["status"]
2599	                error = item.get("error", ERROR_FIELD_UNSET)
2600	                if status == "succeeded":

2602	                        raise RequestInvalidError(
2603	                            "A successful run must not carry an error message"
2604	                        )
2605	                elif error is None or error is ERROR_FIELD_UNSET or not error.strip():
2606	                    raise RequestInvalidError(
2607	                        "A failed run requires a non-empty error message"
2608	                    )
2609	
2610	            # Phase 3: resolve every run. Existence across the whole batch is
2611	            # checked before ownership: a run in another dataset/version is out
2612	            # of scope and reported as not found (404), never as an ownership
2613	            # mismatch.
2614	            run_rows: dict[int, sqlite3.Row] = {}
2615	            for item in items:
2616	                run_id = item["run_id"]
2617	                run_row = conn.execute(
2618	                    "SELECT r.*, t.version_id AS owner_version_id "
2619	                    "FROM processing_task_runs r "
2620	                    "JOIN processing_tasks t ON t.id = r.task_id "
2621	                    "WHERE r.id = ?",
2622	                    (run_id,),
2623	                ).fetchone()
2624	                if run_row is None or run_row["owner_version_id"] != version_row["id"]:
2625	                    raise NotFoundError(
2626	                        f"Processing task run {run_id} does not exist in version "
2627	                        f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
2628	                    )
2629	                run_rows[run_id] = run_row
2630	
2631	            # Phase 4: ownership within the version. A run of another task in
2632	            # the same (dataset, version) is a 422.
2633	            for item in items:
2634	                run_row = run_rows[item["run_id"]]

2640	                    )
2641	
2642	            # Phase 5: conflicts, evaluated only once every reference resolves
2643	            # and every payload is valid (404/422 take precedence, as on the
2644	            # single finish endpoint). The same task may appear at most once;
2645	            # only the task's current running run can be completed and the task
2646	            # must still be running.

2648	            for item in items:
2649	                task_id = item["task_id"]
2650	                if task_id in seen_task_ids:

2653	                        "batch; each task may be completed at most once"
2654	                    )

2661	                        f"Processing task run {run_row['id']} is already "
2662	                        f"'{run_row['status']}' and cannot be finished again"

2664	                if task_row["status"] != "running":
2665	                    raise ConflictError(
2666	                        f"Processing task {task_row['id']} is "
2667	                        f"'{task_row['status']}' and cannot be completed currently"

2672	            # race rolls back the entire batch.

2676	                error = item["error"] if item["status"] == "failed" else None

2678	                    "UPDATE processing_task_runs SET status = ?, finished_at = ?, "
2679	                    "error = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'running'",

2692	            completed: list[dict] = []
2693	            for item in items:
2694	                updated = conn.execute(

2696	                    (item["run_id"],),

2699	        except BaseException:
2700	            conn.rollback()
2701	            raise
2702	
2703	    completed.sort(key=lambda run: run["task_id"])

2705	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
2706	        "version": version_row["version"],

2708	    }

2725	def _task_dependency_graph(rows: list[sqlite3.Row]) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
2726	    """Adjacency task id -> its direct dependency ids for one version."""
2727	    return {row["id"]: json.loads(row["depends_on"]) for row in rows}

2730	def _graph_reaches_target(
2731	    graph: dict[int, list[int]], start: int, target: int
2732	) -> bool:
2733	    """Whether ``target`` is reachable from ``start`` along dependency edges."""
2734	    visited = {start}
2735	    stack = [start]
2736	    while stack:
2737	        current = stack.pop()
2738	        for dependency in graph.get(current, ()):
2739	            if dependency == target:
2740	                return True
2741	            if dependency not in visited:
2742	                visited.add(dependency)
2743	                stack.append(dependency)
2744	    return False

2747	def replace_task_dependencies(
2748	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
2749	    dataset_name: str,
2750	    version_number: int,
2751	    task_id: int,
2752	    depends_on: list[int],
2753	) -> dict:
2754	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
2755	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
2756	    task_row = _require_task(
2757	        conn, version_row, dataset_name, version_number, task_id
2758	    )
2759	
2760	    if len(set(depends_on)) != len(depends_on):
2761	        raise RequestInvalidError("'depends_on' must not contain duplicate task ids")
2762	    if task_id in depends_on:
2763	        raise ConflictError(
2764	            f"Processing task {task_id} must not depend on itself"
2765	        )
2766	
2767	    task_rows = _version_task_rows(conn, version_row["id"])
2768	    existing_ids = {row["id"] for row in task_rows}
2769	    unknown = [dependency_id for dependency_id in depends_on if dependency_id not in existing_ids]
2770	    if unknown:
2771	        raise NotFoundError(
2772	            f"Dependency task {unknown[0]} does not exist in version "
2773	            f"{version_number} of dataset '{dataset_name}'"
2774	        )
2775	
2776	    if task_row["status"] != "pending":
2777	        raise ConflictError(
2778	            f"Processing task {task_id} is '{task_row['status']}'; only pending "
2779	            "tasks can have their dependencies replaced"
2780	        )
2781	
2782	    # Build the prospective graph (the target task's edges replaced, every other
2783	    # task unchanged) and reject cycles. Only the target's edges change, so any
2784	    # newly introduced cycle must pass through the target: it exists iff a new
2785	    # dependency can already reach the target.
2786	    graph = _task_dependency_graph(task_rows)
2787	    graph[task_row["id"]] = list(depends_on)
2788	    if any(
2789	        _graph_reaches_target(graph, dependency_id, task_row["id"])
2790	        for dependency_id in depends_on
2791	    ):
2792	        raise ConflictError(
2793	            "Replacing the dependencies would introduce a cycle in the task graph"
2794	        )
2795	
2796	    # Validation above shares this transaction with the write, so the replacement
2797	    # either commits atomically or leaves the graph untouched.
2798	    conn.execute(
2799	        "UPDATE processing_tasks SET depends_on = ? WHERE id = ?",
2800	        (json.dumps(list(depends_on)), task_row["id"]),
2801	    )
2802	    updated = conn.execute(
2803	        "SELECT * FROM processing_tasks WHERE id = ?", (task_row["id"],)
2804	    ).fetchone()
2805	    return _task_row_to_dict(updated, dataset["name"], version_row["version"])

2808	def _schedule_states(
2809	    graph: dict[int, tuple[str, int, int, list[int]]],
2810	) -> dict[int, str]:
2811	    """Derive the schedule state of every task in one version.
2812	
2813	    Non-pending tasks map directly from their stored status (``failed`` splits
2814	    into ``retryable``/``exhausted`` on remaining attempts). Pending tasks are
2815	    resolved against their dependencies by fixed-point propagation: all direct
2816	    dependencies succeeded -> ``ready``; any dependency chain exhausted or
2817	    already ``upstream_failed`` -> ``upstream_failed``; otherwise ``blocked``.
2818	    The graph is acyclic (enforced at creation and on every replacement), so
2819	    the propagation terminates.
2820	    """
2821	    states: dict[int, str] = {}
2822	    for task_id, (status, attempt_count, max_attempts, _deps) in graph.items():
2823	        if status == "pending":
2824	            continue
2825	        if status == "failed":
2826	            states[task_id] = (
2827	                "retryable" if attempt_count < max_attempts else "exhausted"
2828	            )
2829	        else:
2830	            states[task_id] = status
2831	
2832	    changed = True
2833	    while changed:
2834	        changed = False
2835	        for task_id, (status, _attempt_count, _max_attempts, deps) in graph.items():
2836	            if status != "pending":
2837	                continue
2838	            if any(
2839	                states.get(dependency_id) in ("exhausted", "upstream_failed")
2840	                for dependency_id in deps
2841	            ):
2842	                new_state = "upstream_failed"
2843	            elif all(
2844	                states.get(dependency_id) == "succeeded" for dependency_id in deps
2845	            ):
2846	                # An empty dependency list vacuously satisfies "all succeeded".
2847	                new_state = "ready"
2848	            else:
2849	                new_state = "blocked"
2850	            if states.get(task_id) != new_state:
2851	                states[task_id] = new_state
2852	                changed = True
2853	    return states

2856	def get_processing_schedule(
2857	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int
2858	) -> dict:
2859	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
2860	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
2861	
2862	    rows = _version_task_rows(conn, version_row["id"])
2863	    graph: dict[int, tuple[str, int, int, list[int]]] = {
2864	        row["id"]: (
2865	            row["status"],
2866	            row["attempt_count"],
2867	            row["max_attempts"],
2868	            json.loads(row["depends_on"]),
2869	        )
2870	        for row in rows
2871	    }
2872	    states = _schedule_states(graph)
2873	
2874	    tasks: list[dict] = []
2875	    for row in rows:
2876	        task = _task_row_to_dict(row, dataset["name"], version_row["version"])
2877	        task["schedule_state"] = states[row["id"]]
2878	        if row["status"] == "pending":
2879	            deps = graph[row["id"]][3]
2880	            task["blocking_task_ids"] = sorted(
2881	                dependency_id
2882	                for dependency_id in deps
2883	                if states.get(dependency_id) != "succeeded"
2884	            )
2885	        else:
2886	            task["blocking_task_ids"] = []
2887	        tasks.append(task)
2888
